Definition: to set (literally or figuratively); intensively, to found; reflexively, to sit down together, i.e. settle, consult
BiblicalUsage: The hail that fell on Egypt was such as had not been since the day it was founded, Joshua cursed the man who should rise up and build Jericho and lay its foundation in his firstborn, the king commanded great stones, costly stones, to lay the foundation of the house. David and Samuel ordained the porters in their set office.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that founding is God's word for beginning something meant to last: Egypt was founded, Jericho was founded and cursed, the temple was founded on costly stone, and men were ordained — set in place — for the gates. I believe the foundation is where the rest of the building is decided, and the Bible watches carefully what is laid first.
